with socket.socket() as probe: probe.bind((parsed.hostname,parsed.port))
environment={**os.environ,**plan["start_environment"]}
with (private/"native_stdout.log").open("xb") as stdout,(private/"native_stderr.log").open("xb") as stderr:
    child=subprocess.Popen(meta["planned_command"],cwd=root,env=environment,stdin=subprocess.DEVNULL,
                           stdout=stdout,stderr=stderr,shell=False,start_new_session=True)
    try:
        receipt={**read_process(child.pid),"planned_argv":meta["planned_command"],
                 "binary_sha256":meta["binary_sha256"],"metadata_sha256":plan["deployment"]["metadata_sha256"],
                 "launched_unix_ns":time.time_ns(),"stdout":"native_stdout.log","stderr":"native_stderr.log"}
        save_new(owner_path,receipt)
    except BaseException:
        child.terminate()
        try: child.wait(timeout=5)
        except subprocess.TimeoutExpired: child.kill(); child.wait(timeout=5)
        raise
print(json.dumps({"status":"START_REQUESTED","owner_receipt":str(owner_path),"pid":child.pid,

libc=ctypes.CDLL(None,use_errno=True)
events=[]
for signum in (signal.SIGTERM,signal.SIGKILL):
    observed=state(owner)

execution_sequence: Only after the root coordinates the reserved installation phase, execute commands.start.argv directly without a shell. It verifies the pinned binary digest and a free loopback port, uses the unchanged deployment argv and resource environment, and records a new PID/start-time receipt.

Execute commands.status.argv without HTTP. Require the PID/start identity, executable and argv to match, affinity to remain within CPUs 2 and 3, and the expected loopback listener with no non-loopback owned TCP listeners.

If startup exits, the listener boundary is unestablished, affinity is wrong, or later shutdown is requested, use commands.stop.argv. It sends bounded SIGTERM then SIGKILL only through a pidfd after matching the recorded identity and executable/argv.

Keep native logs, ownership receipts and stop receipts private. Before any subsequent start, archive the preceding stopped instance receipt and logs without overwriting them; the start command deliberately refuses existing files.
Do not run this background-start launcher inside a command meter that cleans its descendants when the launcher exits; use the installer-owned process receipt for lifecycle supervision.

Account provisioning, baseline preparation and assessment scheduling remain separate future installation/evaluation work. This plan authors no business goals, UI routes, selectors or operation schemas.
stop_scope: The one recorded native process; no broad process-group, name-based, or container stop operation.
